stories-27-38-44-queen-of-sheba-throne-c.title: The Queen of Sheba Taking Solomon's Glass Palace Floor for Deep Water
stories-27-38-44-queen-of-sheba-throne-c.note: Surah 27:38–44 culminates with the Queen of Sheba entering Solomon's palace, supposing its polished crystal floor is a pool of water, and uncovering her legs, matching the Aramaic glass-house narrative in Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2.

discussion.view: Muslim commentators such as al-Tabari and al-Qurtubi treat the crystal pavilion and the uncovering of the Queen's legs as historical events from Solomon's royal court in Jerusalem.
discussion.reply: First Kings 10:1–13 and 2 Chronicles 9:1–12 record the Queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon without any mention of a glass floor, a hoopoe messenger, or the Queen lifting her garments over water. That sequence comes from the Galilean Aramaic Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2, an aggadic expansion of Solomon's court.

stories-27-38-44-queen-of-sheba-throne-c.quranEn: [38] He said, ‘Assembly! Which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in surrender?’ [39] A crafty one of the jinn said, ‘I shall bring it to you before you (can) rise from your place. Surely I have strength for it (and am) trustworthy.’ [40] One who had knowledge of the Book said, ‘I will bring it to you in the wink of an eye.’ So when he saw it set before him, he said, ‘This is from the favor of my Lord to test me (to see) whether I am thankful or ungrateful. Whoever is thankful is thankful only for his own good, and whoever is ungrateful – surely my Lord is wealthy, generous.’ [41] He said, ‘Disguise her throne for her. We shall see whether she is (rightly) guided or is one of those who are not (rightly) guided.’ [42] So when she came, it was said, ‘Is your throne like this?’ She said, ‘It seems like it.’ ‘And we had been given the knowledge before her, and were in surrender, [43] but what she served, instead of God, kept her back. Surely she was from a disbelieving people.’ [44] It was said to her, ‘Enter the palace.’ When she saw it, she thought it was a pool (of water), and she uncovered her legs. He said, ‘Surely it is a polished palace of crystal.’ She said, ‘My Lord, surely I have done myself evil. I surrender with Solomon to God, Lord of the worlds.’
quranHighlights: It was said to her, ‘Enter the palace.’ When she saw it, she thought it was a pool (of water), and she uncovered her legs. He said, ‘Surely it is a polished palace of crystal.’

sources.title: Targum Sheni on Esther
sources.en: When King Solomon heard that she had come to him, King Solomon rose and went and sat in a house of glass. She thought in her heart that the king was sitting in water, and she lifted her skirts to cross over, and he saw that there was hair on her legs. King Solomon said, “Your beauty is the beauty of women, but your hair is the hair of a man. Hair is becoming to a man but shameful to a woman.”
highlights: King Solomon rose and went and sat in a house of glass.
She thought in her heart that the king was sitting in water, and she lifted her skirts to cross over

stories-27-20-28-solomon-missing-hoopoe-.title: Solomon Reviewing the Birds, the Missing Hoopoe, and News from Sheba
stories-27-20-28-solomon-missing-hoopoe-.note: Surah 27:20–28 narrates Solomon inspecting his birds, threatening the absent hoopoe (hudhud), hearing its report on the sun-worshipping Queen of Sheba, and dispatching a letter by bird, reproducing Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that Solomon employed the hoopoe as a scout to locate underground water during his military marches and sent it with a royal letter summoning Bilqis, the Queen of Sheba, to submit to God.
discussion.reply: In 1 Kings 10:1–2, the Queen of Sheba hears of Solomon's fame and travels to Jerusalem without any bird messenger. In the Galilean Aramaic Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2, Solomon misses the wild cock (hoopoe) during a feast, threatens to destroy it in anger, hears its report of a wealthy eastern city ruled by the Queen of Sheba, and binds a letter to its wing.

stories-27-20-28-solomon-missing-hoopoe-.quranEn: [20] He reviewed the birds, and said, ‘Why do I not see the hudhud? Or is it one of the absent? [21] I shall indeed punish it severely, or slaughter it, or it will bring me a clear authority.’ [22] But it did not stay (away) for long, and said, ‘I have encompassed what you have not encompassed, and I have brought you reliable news from (the people of) Sheba. [23] Surely I found a woman ruling over them, and she has been given (some) of everything, and she has a great throne. [24] I found her and her people prostrating themselves before the sun instead of God. Satan has made their deeds appear enticing to them, and he has kept them from the way, and they are not (rightly) guided. [25] (He did this) so that they would not prostrate themselves before God, who brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and the earth. He knows what you hide and what you speak aloud. [26] God – (there is) no god but Him, Lord of the great throne.’ [27] He said, ‘We shall see whether you have spoken the truth or are one of the liars. [28] Go with this letter of mine, and cast it (down) to them. Then turn away from them and see what they return.’

I have brought you reliable news from (the people of) Sheba. [23] Surely I found a woman ruling over them

sources.title: Targum Sheni on Esther
sources.ref: Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2 (Report on Sheba)
sources.en: I looked and saw a country in the land of the East; Kitor is the name of its city. Its dust is more precious than gold, and silver lies like dung in its streets. Trees have stood planted there since the beginning of the world, and they drink water from the Garden of Eden. Great multitudes live there with crowns on their heads, planted there from the Garden of Eden. They do not know how to fight in battle, and they cannot shoot with the bow. But truly I saw one woman who rules over all of them, and her name is the Queen of Sheba.
highlights: I looked and saw a country in the land of the East; Kitor is the name of its city.
Its dust is more precious than gold, and silver lies like dung in its streets
But truly I saw one woman who rules over all of them, and her name is the Queen of Sheba.

sources.title: Targum Sheni on Esther
sources.ref: Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2 (Letter Tied to Wing)
sources.en: The king’s scribes were summoned, and they wrote a letter and tied the letter to the wing of the wild rooster. It rose and went up into the heights of the sky, whirled aloft, gathered its strength and flew among the birds, and they flew after it, and they went to the city of Kitor, to the land of Sheba. In the morning the Queen of Sheba went out to worship the sea, and the birds darkened the sun. She took hold of her clothes and tore them, and she was utterly astonished. While she was utterly astonished, the wild rooster came down to her, and she saw that a letter was tied to its wing.

stories-27-15-19-solomon-speech-of-birds.title: Solomon Taught the Speech of Birds and Hearing the Ant in the Valley
stories-27-15-19-solomon-speech-of-birds.note: Surah 27:15–19 states that Solomon was taught the speech of birds (mantiq al-tayr), marshaled ranks of jinn, men, and birds, and understood an ant warning its colony, matching Solomon's rule over birds and demons in Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that God granted Solomon miraculous comprehension of animal and avian languages alongside command over jinn and human armies, enabling him to hear the queen ant warning her colony as his forces marched past.
discussion.reply: In 1 Kings 4:33, Solomon composes proverbs concerning trees, beasts, birds, and creeping things. Late antique Jewish exegesis in Targum Sheni on Esther 1:2 and Talmud Bavli Gittin 68a transforms this botanical and zoological wisdom into literal sovereignty over wild beasts, birds of the sky, and demons (shedim), explicitly stating that Solomon knew the speech of all of them and they understood his speech.

stories-27-15-19-solomon-speech-of-birds.quranEn: [15] Certainly We gave David and Solomon knowledge, and they said, ‘Praise (be) to God, who has favored us over many of His believing servants!’ [16] Solomon inherited (it) from David, and said, ‘People! We have been taught the speech of birds, and we have been given (some) of everything. Surely this – it indeed is clear favor.’ [17] Gathered before Solomon were his forces – jinn, and men, and birds – and they were arranged (in rows) [18] – until, when they came upon the Wādī of the Ants, an ant said, ‘Ants! Enter your dwellings, or Solomon and his forces will crush you without realizing (it).’ [19] But he smiled, laughing at its words, and said, ‘My Lord, (so) dispose me that I may be thankful for your blessing with which You have blessed me and my parents, and that I may do righteousness (that) pleases You, and cause me to enter, by Your mercy, among your righteous servants.’

sources.title: Targum Sheni on Esther
sources.en: After David rose Solomon his son, whom the Holy One, blessed be he, made king over the wild beasts, over the birds of the sky, over all the earth, and over demons, spirits and liliths. He knew the speech of all of them, and they understood his speech, for so it is written, “He spoke of trees.”
